title: Malacañang calls for probe into alleged coercion of VP Sara Duterte's ex-staff
summary: Malacañang said Tuesday authorities should investigate the claims of the camp of Vice President Sara Duterte that her former household help was allegedly coerced to sign a document.

blocks.text: Malacañang said Tuesday authorities should investigate the claims of the camp of Vice President Sara Duterte that her former household help was allegedly coerced to sign a document.
“Ang pag-iimbestiga sa nasabing kwento kung may katotohanan ay nararapat lamang,” Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro said in a statement.
(It’s only fitting to investigate the claims to determine if there is any truth to it.)

Atty. Paolo Panelo, spokesperson for Duterte, said that the Vice President received a message "from what appeared to be the account of a former household staff member" at 11:19 pm on Monday, November 16.
He said the message contained “a desperate plea for help and rescue” in Manila.

“The sender claimed to be in the custody or under the control of certain individuals who allegedly told them about a threat to their life. The former staff member further narrated that they were being forced to sign a document, which they had refused to execute,” Panelo said.

He said the Vice President’s camp is deeply concerned that the alleged incident may be part of a supposed “relentless campaign by the Marcos administration, utilizing state institutions like the NBI, against the Vice President.”
Castro, for Malacañang’s part, shrugged off the allegation, saying the President is currently busy with the ASEAN Summit.

“Buhos ang oras ng Pangulo sa pagtatrabaho para sa ikakaunlad ng bansa at sa pagpapatibay ng magandang ugnayan sa mga member states ng ASEAN at mga dialogue partners. Pagpapaayos ng ekonomiya, solusyon sa usaping enerhiya, teknolohiya, agrikultura, at edukasyon ang tinututukan ng ating Pangulo,” she said.

(The President is dedicating his time to the nation’s development and strengthening positive relations with ASEAN member-states and dialogue partners. He is focusing on improving the economy, as well as addressing issues related to energy, technology, agriculture, and education.)
Castro also stressed that Marcos does not resort to doing such tactics.

“Hindi po gawain sa panahon ngayon ang gumawa ng intriga at magplanta ng ebidensya kung saan sanay at hasa ang Duterte administration at ito naman ay inamin noon pa ni dating Pangulong Duterte sa harapan ng media,” she added.

(The administration does not stir up such allegations or plant evidence—tactics in which the Duterte administration is well-versed and highly skilled, as former President Duterte himself previously admitted before the media.) —KG, GMA News
